title: Industrial Relations Officer
summary: Industrial relations (IR) officers manage the relationship between a factory's management, its workers and their unions. They sit in the plant HR team and handle union talks, grievances, disciplinary enquiries, contract labour and compliance with factory and labour laws.
dailyDuties: Meet union representatives and resolve shop-floor grievances
Draft charge sheets and conduct domestic enquiries
Audit labour contractors for licences, registers and wage payments
Maintain Factories Act registers and file returns
Review canteen, transport and welfare facilities with committees
Prepare data for wage settlement negotiations
Attend meetings with labour department officials

skills.expectation: Prepare for and take part in union negotiations and long-term wage settlements
Handle worker grievances on the shop floor and keep relations with unions stable
Draft charge sheets and show cause notices and run domestic enquiries under the standing orders
Manage contractors and keep contract labour licences, registers and wage payments compliant
Keep the plant compliant with the Factories Act and OSH Code: licence, registers, returns and inspections
Apply the labour codes on wages, PF, ESI, bonus and gratuity for plant workers
Run canteen, transport and other statutory welfare facilities and committees
Talk with workers, union leaders and managers in English, Hindi or the local language
Represent the plant before labour officers and in conciliation
Check attendance and wage inputs from the time office
Keep worker records in the HRMS
Organise engagement and safety-week events for workers
Keep IR trackers and compliance calendars in Excel
